Optional statement to reduce the amount of nesting without having to modify the Cluster SQL statement
SET CLUSTER LEVEL LIMIT = 5
Create the clusters and nodes

SELECT [Cloud]              AS [CLUSTER1], 
       'AWS Cloud'          AS [CLUSTER1 LABEL],
       'Cloud'              AS [CLUSTER1 STYLE NAME],

       [Data Center]        AS [CLUSTER2], 
       [Data Center]        AS [CLUSTER2 LABEL], 
       'Data Center'        AS [CLUSTER2 STYLE NAME],
 
       [VPC]                AS [CLUSTER3],
       'VPC'                AS [CLUSTER3 LABEL], 
       'VPC'                AS [CLUSTER3 STYLE NAME],

       [AZ Cluster]         AS [CLUSTER4],
       [AZ Cluster]         AS [CLUSTER4 LABEL], 
       'AZ Cluster'         AS [CLUSTER4 STYLE NAME],
 
       [AZ Id]              AS [CLUSTER5],
       'Availability Zone'  AS [CLUSTER5 LABEL], 
       'Availability zone'  AS [CLUSTER5 STYLE NAME],
 
       [Node]               AS [Item],
       [Node Type]          AS [Label],     
       [Node Type]          AS [Style Name],
       1                    AS [Split Length] 
FROM [ComponentList$]
WHERE [Node] IS NOT NULL
Create the edges

SELECT [Node From]       AS [Item], 
       [Node To]         AS [Related Item], 
       [Caption]         AS [Label], 
       [Connection Type] AS [Style Name] 
FROM   [ComponentList$]
WHERE  [Node From] IS NOT NULL
AND    [Node To]   IS NOT NULL

Specify the workbook containing the data
SET DATA FILE
Set placeholder values for substitution into SQL. Wrap placeholder name in braces in the SQL.
SET PLACEHOLDER placeholder_name = value

For example, to query for records matching the value "Metropolitan", assign Metropolitan to a placeholder, 
then use the placeholder name wrapped in braces in the SQL as static text in WHERE comparisons, label, or tooltip text.
SET PLACEHOLDER subway_line = Metropolitan

SELECT [station_from] AS [Item], [station_to] AS [Related Item], '{subway_line} Line' AS [Label], 
FROM   [london_underground$]
WHERE  [tube_route] = '{subway_line}'
Create the edges

SELECT [From Column] AS [Item], 
       [To Column]   AS [Related Item] 
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
Create the nodes

SELECT [Node Id Column]    AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column] AS [Label],
       [Node Style Column] AS [Style Name]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$] 
WHERE  ...
Create edges which chain a set of nodes

SELECT [Node Id Column] AS [ITEM], 
       TRUE             AS [CREATE EDGES]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
WHERE  ...
Create a subgraph, with rank= constraint specified as either 'same' | 'min' | 'source' | 'max' | 'sink'.

The rank attribute tells Graphviz how to line up the nodes inside a subgraph:
- rank=same   - all nodes sit on the same horizontal (or vertical) level.
- rank=min    - all nodes are pushed to the top (or left) of the graph.
- rank=source - same as min, but Graphviz also ensures that only subgraphs marked source or min share that top/left rank.
- rank=max    - all nodes are pushed to the bottom (or right) of the graph.
- rank=sink   - same as max, but restricted to subgraphs marked sink or max.
NOTE: Graphviz treats the minimum rank as the top/left edge of the layout and the maximum rank as the bottom/right edge.

SELECT [Node Id Column] AS [ITEM], 
       TRUE             AS [CREATE RANK],
       'same'           AS [RANK]
FROM   [Worksheet Name$]
WHERE  ...
Split text for labels at first blank after 10 characters

SELECT [Label Column] AS [Label],
       10             AS [SPLIT LENGTH],
       ...
Specify the line ending (\l, \n, \r, | etc.) to use when splitting a label

SELECT [Label Column] AS [Label],
       10             AS [SPLIT LENGTH],
       '\r'           AS [LINE ENDING],
       ...
Multi-level - Group nodes into nested clusters. "n" levels of nesting supported, within max level limit on settings sheet

SELECT [Cluster 1 Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER1],
       [Cluster 1 Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER1 LABEL],
       [Cluster 1 Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER1 STYLE NAME],
       [Cluster 1 Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER1 ATTRIBUTES],
       [Cluster 1 Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER1 TOOLTIP],

       [Cluster 2 Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER2],
       [Cluster 2 Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER2 LABEL],
       [Cluster 2 Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER2 STYLE NAME],
       [Cluster 2 Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER2 ATTRIBUTES],
       [Cluster 2 Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER2 TOOLTIP],

       [Node Id Column]              AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]           AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]      AS [Style Name],
       ...
Specifies the number of cluster nestings permitted. Useful for folding clusters together without modifying the Cluster SQL statement.
SET CLUSTER LEVEL LIMIT = 10
LEGACY - Group nodes into a cluster

SELECT [Cluster Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER],
       [Cluster Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER LABEL],
       [Cluster Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Cluster Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER TOOLTIP],
       [Node Id Column]            AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]         AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]    AS [Style Name],
       ...
LEGACY - Group nodes into two level clusters

SELECT [Outer Cluster Id Column]         AS [CLUSTER],
       [Outer Cluster Label Column]      AS [CLUSTER LABEL],
       [Outer Cluster Style Name Column] AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Outer Cluster Attributes]        AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Outer Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [CLUSTER TOOLTIP],

       [Inner Cluster Id Column]         AS [SUBCLUSTER],
       [Inner Cluster Label Column]      AS [SUBCLUSTER LABEL],
       [Inner Cluster Style Name Column] AS [SUBCLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       [Inner Cluster Attributes]        AS [SUBCLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       [Inner Cluster Tooltip Column]    AS [SUBCLUSTER TOOLTIP],

       [Node Id Column]                  AS [Item],
       [Node Label Column]               AS [Label],
       [Node Style Name Column]          AS [Style Name],
       ...

Loop count substitution strings (useful in sortv= attributes, style names, and labels). 
  {clc}   = Cluster count     / Absolute cluster number
  {scc}   = Subcluster count  / Relative cluster number within the parent cluster
  {rsc}   = Record set count
  {level} = Level/depth of cluster nesting (Multi-level clustering only; not available in LEGACY clustering).

SELECT 'sortv={clc}'    AS [CLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       'Border {clc} '  AS [CLUSTER STYLE NAME],
       'sortv={scc}'    AS [SUBCLUSTER ATTRIBUTES],
       'sortv={rsc}'    AS [Attributes],
       ...
FROM   [Worksheet Name$] 
WHERE  ...
ORDER BY [Outer Cluster Label Column] ASC,
         [Inner Cluster Label Column] ASC,
         [Node Label Column]          ASC
Enumerate a range to create nodes (e.g. For 1 to 5 by 1).

SELECT TRUE AS [ENUMERATE],
       MIN(CLng([some-column])) AS [START AT],
       MAX(CLng([some-column])) AS [STOP AT],
       1                        AS [STEP BY],
       '{step}'                 AS [Item],
       '{step}'                 AS [Label],
       'some-style'             AS [Style Name]
FROM [some-table$]
WHERE IsNumeric([some-column])
Enumerate a range to create a chain of edges (e.g. For 1 to 5 by 1). See "CREATE EDGES" above.

SELECT TRUE AS [CREATE EDGES],
       TRUE AS [ENUMERATE],
       MIN(CLng([some-column])) AS [START AT],
       MAX(CLng([some-column])) AS [STOP AT],
       1                        AS [STEP BY],
       '{step}'                 AS [Item]
FROM [some-table$]
WHERE IsNumeric([some-column])

ITERATE - For Header-Detail situations. Run a SQL statement to generate the ID values of the header records. For each ID value in the header, run a SQL statement. Generally used in situations where you need to process the data in chunks such as creating subgroups, or combining the values of multiple records into a single string.

SELECT 
  'SELECT [some-column] AS [ID] FROM [some-table$]' AS [SQL FOR ID],
  'SELECT [another-column] AS [ITEM], FROM [another-table$] WHERE [some-other-column] = ''{ID}'' ' AS [SQL FOR DATA],
  TRUE AS [ITERATE]
ITERATE with CREATE RANK - Create subgraphs for each ID returned in the SQL FOR ID query. See "CREATE RANK" above.

SELECT 
  'SELECT [some-column] AS [ID] FROM [some-table$]' AS [SQL FOR ID],
  'SELECT [some-column] AS [ITEM], TRUE AS [CREATE RANK], ''same'' AS [RANK] FROM [another-table$] WHERE [some-other-column] = ''{ID}'' ' AS [SQL FOR DATA],
  TRUE AS [ITERATE]

ITERATE with CONCATENATE - Build nodes, where each node lists all the matching records on separate lines within the label of a rectangle (due to \n separator). The fields emitted to the data worksheet are specified in the first SQL statement [SQL FOR ID]. (NOTE:The SQL passed as parameters has been kept to one line to reduce confusion).

SELECT 
  TRUE       AS [ITERATE],
  'SELECT DISTINCT [some-column] AS [ID], [some-column] AS [Item], [another-column] AS [Label], ''shape=rectangle'' AS [Attributes] FROM [some-table$]' 
             AS [SQL FOR ID],
  'SELECT [another-column] AS [Label] FROM [some-table$] WHERE [some-column] = ''{ID}'' AND [some-column] IS NOT NULL'                                 
             AS [SQL FOR DATA],
  TRUE       AS [CONCATENATE],
  'Label'    AS [FIELD],
  'Label'    AS [ASSIGN TO], 
  ''         AS [PREFIX], 
  ''         AS [SUFFIX], 
  '\n'       AS [SEPARATOR]

ITERATE with CONCATENATE - Build nodes, where each node lists all the matching records on separate cells within the label of a record (due to | separator). The fields emitted to the data worksheet are specified in the first SQL statement [SQL FOR ID]. (NOTE:The SQL passed as parameters has been kept to one line to reduce confusion).

SELECT 
  TRUE       AS [ITERATE],
  'SELECT DISTINCT [some-column] AS [ID], [some-column] AS [Item], [another-column] AS [Label], ''shape=record'' AS [Attributes] FROM [some-table$]' 
             AS [SQL FOR ID],
  'SELECT [another-column] AS [Label] FROM [some-table$] WHERE [some-column] = ''{ID}'' AND [some-column] IS NOT NULL'                                 
             AS [SQL FOR DATA],
  TRUE       AS [CONCATENATE],
  'Label'    AS [FIELD],
  'Label'    AS [ASSIGN TO], 
  '{'        AS [PREFIX], 
  '}'        AS [SUFFIX], 
  '|'        AS [SEPARATOR]
Show the graph immediately after all SQL statements processed
PREVIEW [ AS ( DIRECTED | UNDIRECTED ) GRAPH ]
Publish graphs as files
PUBLISH [ ALL VIEWS ] [ AS ( DIRECTED | UNDIRECTED ) GRAPH ] [ file prefix ]

buttons.superTip: The table gives the name of the attribute, the graph components (node, edge, etc.) which use the attribute and the type of the attribute (strings representing legal values of that type). Where applicable, the table also gives a default value for the attribute, a minimum allowed setting for numeric attributes, and certain restrictions on the use of the attribute.
